claims.text: Pure elemental Cr coatings protect zirconium-alloy cladding under both normal subcritical-water and accident-relevant high-temperature steam conditions.
High-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
A Cr coating can be modified by incorporating 1–5 at.% Al to form an Al-alloyed Cr coating.
A small Al addition will promote in situ formation of a continuous alumina-rich or Cr–Al composite oxide layer.
Al preferentially oxidizes during service to form Al2O3 or a mixed Cr–Al oxide.
The proposed alumina-rich or Cr–Al oxide layer is stable and dense.
The proposed alumina-rich or Cr–Al oxide is more refractory and less permeable than pure chromium oxide.
The proposed oxide layer acts as a diffusion barrier between the Cr coating and the Zr substrate.
The diffusion barrier will slow Cr transport into the zirconium substrate and reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve coating integrity and mitigate premature high-temperature coating degradation.
Relative to pure Cr, the Al-doped Cr coating will have improved oxidation resistance at accident temperatures.
Relative to pure Cr, the Al-doped coating will exhibit less premature failure by spallation or cracking.
The Al-doped Cr coating will maintain corrosion resistance in simulated PWR primary water near 300°C.
The intervention is applicable to accident-relevant high-temperature steam at approximately 1000–1100°C or above.
The intervention is applicable across both extended normal-service exposures and short accident transients.
